questions.q: Why does requesting the broadest available OAuth scope "just in case it's needed later" violate least privilege, even if that extra access is never actually used?
options: It doesn't violate least privilege, since unused access carries no risk
If the token is ever leaked or the app is compromised, the blast radius is as large as the scope allows — regardless of whether the extra access was ever actually exercised
Broad scopes are always rejected by Salesforce automatically
Least privilege only applies to user accounts, not OAuth tokens
questions.explain: Least privilege is about limiting potential damage if access is ever misused or stolen, not about whether the extra access has been exercised yet.

questions.q: What security problem does storing a secret in a Named Credential instead of hardcoding it in Apex code solve?
options: It makes the Apex code run faster
It eliminates the need for any authentication at all
It keeps the secret out of version control and every code copy, and lets a compromised secret be rotated as a configuration change instead of a code deployment
It converts the callout into a SOAP call automatically
questions.explain: A hardcoded secret ends up anywhere the code exists; a Named Credential centralizes it declaratively, making rotation simple and keeping it out of the codebase.

questions.q: What do Trusted IP Ranges / login IP restrictions limit?
options: Which OAuth scopes an app can request
How many records a query can return
Which API version a client must use
Which network locations a login or API call is allowed to originate from
questions.explain: IP restrictions reduce the usefulness of a stolen credential or token to an attacker operating from outside the trusted network ranges.

questions.q: Why should an integration still validate inbound data even if it arrived through an authenticated channel?
options: Authentication proves who is calling, but doesn't guarantee what they're sending is well-formed or safe
Validation is unnecessary once authentication has succeeded
Authenticated channels cannot carry malformed data by definition
Only unauthenticated channels need validation
questions.explain: Authentication establishes identity, not the correctness or safety of the payload itself — those are separate concerns that still need handling.

questions.q: What is the security benefit of the 2026 shift from Connected Apps to External Client Apps (ECAs), per this lesson?
options: ECAs eliminate the need for OAuth scopes entirely
ECAs separate an app's identity from its policies (scopes, IP ranges, session behavior) more cleanly, making access easier to audit and tighten
ECAs remove the need for Named Credentials
ECAs are purely a rebranding with no functional security difference
questions.explain: The cleaner separation between an app's core identity and the policies governing it makes it easier for admins to audit and adjust an integration's access without disturbing its registration.
